items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — I can imagine Hiromi marveling at all those 70s classics that influenced her. The good thing is that the 80s also influenced her, and she has room for everything in her musical world. That includes fusions with sounds from other parts of the world, which brings us to her collaboration with Edmar Castaneda, a Colombian harpist. And while the Paraguayan harp is world-renowned, he is a great performer who has given it his own energetic imprint, with colors that vary like the rainbow?sometimes jazzy, sometimes folky, sometimes ethereal and spacey, and other times earthy. In "A Harp In New York," he acts as a guitar, accompanying Hiromi's rapid improvisations, and as always, she brings the joy and happiness of playing, which is evident and captured on tape. The harp's echo is unique; it lingers in the air, its resonance filling the space like no other instrument.For Jaco begins as if with a bass...which he does with the harp, achieving a most original tribute, reaching those very low tones. And together they build endless routes...that sometimes cross, touch, exchange paths, go through tunnels, bridges over rivers, Hiromi does solos with the support of Edmar, who then makes the harp sound like a double bass, and later a guitar until Hiromi joins again.Moonlight Sunshine is that other dimension, the classical dimension they handle so well... and which is also just a step away from indigenous folklore, as Keith Jarrett also demonstrated with his trio. Here the harp sounds like a charango or ukulele, and those solo notes slow down time and even make it rewind, taking each listener to a place as unique as it is personal. And Hiromi seems to accompany at times as if with a Chopin Mazurka.John Williams' bee bop version of Cantina Bar, composed for Star Wars, showcases the duo's playful side, while also making room for virtuosity and a welcome Latin digression that makes it unique, with its cascades of notes that let the sun shine through.The Elements Suite logically consists of four parts, each dedicated to one of the four elements. "Air" features very emotive duets, and it's a pleasure to recognize notes from one of Hiromi's mentors, Chick Corea, both in the structural complexities and in the more emotional ones, as the balance lies precisely in the interplay between the two. Edmar Castaneda is equally impressive in his interpretation, carrying the harmonies on his own as well as accompanying Hiromi's parts, who displays her entire repertoire. "Earth" gives the impression of digging deep, extracting all the possibilities of the harp/piano duet, whether through opposition or superimposition. If there's one thing that distinguishes Hiromi from other pianists, beyond her technical prowess, it's her ability to move the listener, to connect with them, as well as her intelligence in choosing her repertoire.While "Earth" was violent and even aggressive, not wanting to go unnoticed, "Water" is the complete opposite, and what better way to illustrate the calm and undisturbed depths of the sea than with the notes of the harp? There's also room for Hiromi to improvise."Fire" is the most experimental, the most atonal, throwing notes into the air...like cries that will later take sonic form in rapid sequences of notes from both harp and piano. Almost as if they were taking turns in the style of John McLaughlin's Mahavishnu Orchestra...and yet when Hiromi is left alone she reminds me of Friedrich Gulda when he played jazz, with that touch that only those who also know classical music can have.A delightful surprise with Astor Piazzolla's Libertango for the finale, and an arrangement that fits it perfectly. The audience exclaims upon recognizing it; first Edmar plays it, accompanied by Hiromi, and then Hiromi takes over, creating variations on it (something Astor, being a jazz lover, would have loved). And of course, the final section features the two of them together, violent, dramatic, and emotional, virtuosic, and even bloody, going off-key just as the maestro liked.
items._genre: jazz fusion / world music / improvisation / avant-garde
items._cn_summary: 这张现场专辑是上原广美与哥伦比亚竖琴演奏家Edmar Castaneda的合作录音，将钢琴与拉丁竖琴并置为非常规的二重奏配置。竖琴在此不只承担和声功能，还被转化为低音、吉他、charango、ukulele等多种音色声响，拓宽了乐器的表现边界。曲目涵盖原创作品、电影音乐改编（Jaco致敬、Star Wars Cantina Band比波普版本）以及古典语汇的即兴转化。评论重点关注两位演奏者之间的动态对话——即兴路线的交织与分离、情绪从暴力到抒情的快速转换，以及上原在技术之外传递情感与连接听众的能力。整体呈现一种跨文化、跨类型的融合实验，竖琴的共鸣特性被深入开发，与钢琴形成独特对话。

items.body: Review by Sean Trane — I just learned that Black Dance can be considered as the first album of the "coffee" trilogy" andgiven the bark-brown dominated artworks of Picture Music (North Am release) and Time Wind, thiscould be the reason. Those three sleeves are designed by Urs Amann, strongly influenced by SalvadorDali and these paintings fit quite well Klaus' music of those three albums.There are two other reasons why this album is special, one being Klaus' first "synth" album, butalso the presence of a male vocal on the album-closing Voices Of Syn. We're talking of low-rangedtenor Ernst Walter Siemon, which is quite a change, but to be honest, while impressive performanceit is, the track is not enthralling, somewhat overstaying its welcome, because ideas are notprogressing fast enough. Quite frankly, the same can be said of the whole album, but it's stillquite a good album, though I've ended popping out the disc before it's over.
items._cn_summary: 克洛泽·舒尔茨的《Blackdance》被视为其"咖啡"三部曲的开端，封面由受达利影响的画家乌尔斯·阿曼操刀，深褐色基调与专辑音乐气质高度契合。作为舒尔茨首张以合成器为主导的专辑，作品跨越了从氛围铺陈到节奏实验的多个段落。专辑以器乐为主，结尾的《Voices Of Syn》罕见地引入低男高音恩斯特·西蒙的人声，虽演唱极具表现力，但因乐思推进过缓而显得冗长。整体来看，专辑概念完整、制作精良，但部分段落创意推进速度偏慢，听众可能在曲目结束前便选择中断播放。作为德国电子音乐先驱在1974年的探索性作品，它在合成器运用与氛围建构上展现了前瞻性，但在节奏与结构张力上仍存在打磨空间。

items.body: Review by Sean Trane — Ambitious second album that goes double, with four 20-mins+ tracks, and one for each side. WithIrrlicht, Schulze had proven that he could carry out a project all by himself , after having startedsome of the most groundbreaking project with Froese (Tangerine Dream) and Ash Ra Tempel, both ofwhich were the embryos of the future Berlin School of electronic music (also called KosmischeMuziek).As we will see in his future albums, Klaus was cramming a lot of music o,to one disc side and thewhole affair lasts 105+ mins (the CD reissue from 2006 packs in another 55' as a bonus track - livein Brussels in 77), with admittedly only a Farsifa organ, a VCS3 and percussions and the help of anorchestraBack then, Klaus was certainly at the forefront of the groundbreaking of the electronic continent,with only Froese's Tangerine Dream as sole competition, but today, his music is a bit conventionaland dare I say one-dimensional. Where TD were working at three to fill in their albums, Schulze wasalone and often stretching some of his musical ideas a bit too long, but thankfully, he never really overstayed his welcome. He will do much better in a few years, though.
items._genre: progressive electronic / kosmische musik / berlin school
items._cn_summary: 克劳斯·舒尔策在1973年发行的第二张个人专辑是其雄心之作，以双碟形式承载四首二十分钟以上的长篇电子乐作品。舒尔ze仅使用Farfisa管风琴、VCS3合成器、打击乐器与一支管弦乐队，便构建出长达105分钟以上的音响空间。作为柏林学派电子音乐的奠基人之一，他与塔兰格拉之梦的弗罗泽并称为该流派的先驱。专辑呈现出单一演奏者在电子乐器上进行密集探索的创作模式，将合成器音色与管弦乐融合，体现出70年代初电子音乐从极简氛围向结构化长篇的过渡。乐评指出其音乐在当时具有前沿性，但以今日标准审视略显单一维度，舒尔ze在数年后才达到更成熟的水准。

items.body: It marks the Australian artist's second full-length release for Thrill Jockey Photo by David Walker Jules Reidy is releasing a new album through Thrill Jockey, titled Clerestory. Spanning six tracks, the new record arrives off the back of 2025's Ghost/Spirit, which marks the Australian artist's first full-length release for their current label home. Clerestory, a press release said, is different from the "dense song-constructs" of Reidy's previous record, and features one extended piece, made with US strings collective JACK Quartet, as well as five shorter solo pieces. "Clerestory explores a harmonic world built from collections of pitches related to one another as a tone and its shadow," Reidy said in a statement. "In 'Shadow Symmetric', realised by JACK Quartet, these harmonic relationships give rise to... The post Jules Reidy Details New Album, ‘Clerestory’ appeared first on The Quietus.
items._cn_summary: 澳大利亚艺术家Jules Reidy通过Thrill Jockey厂牌发行第二张全长专辑《Clerestory》，收录六首作品。专辑与前作《Ghost/Spirit》风格不同，放弃了密集的歌曲结构，转而呈现更开阔的声学空间。核心亮点是与美国弦乐四重奏JACK Quartet合作的一首长篇作品《Shadow Symmetric》，以及五首独奏短曲。Reidy自述专辑探索了一种由'音调及其影子'构成的谐和世界，音高之间以对称关系相连，形成独特的和声语言。这种基于音高集合的对称和声概念显示出扎实的现代作曲理论基础，同时弦乐四重奏的编制也为抽象和声提供了具象的表达载体。整体方向偏向当代古典与实验音乐的交汇地带。

items.body: Shanghai's underground is like a washing machine that never stops, says Jonas Klein, as he presents an in-depth report on the city's extraordinary musical infrastructure, and picks out five key releases - from the former pop star re-booting the Bristol sound to a hell-bath of distorted drone Shanghai Qiutian "Another one of these, please," I tell the bartender in Chinese, pointing at their self-brewed beer. I look down at my cup and see this slogan: "Shanghai is a bitch, Shanghai is a washing machine". I chuckle at the image. It’s odd, but somehow it all makes sense: this bar, the OKOK Club, is where Shanghai's underground spins its dirty laundry clean. New bands, old punks, foreigners, locals, passers-by, tumbled together until something... The post The Quietus International: Shanghai’s Underground Music, Reviewed by Jonas Klein appeared first on The Quietus.
items._cn_summary: 本文聚焦上海地下音乐场景，以OKOK Club为切入点，呈现了上海作为亚洲地下音乐重镇的多元生态。文章提及五张关键专辑，涵盖前流行明星重启Bristol声响的作品，以及Shanghai Qiutian的失真drone密集噪音轰炸。整体描述带有强烈的场景感，将上海的地下音乐比作永不停歇的洗衣机，暗示其粗糙、混沌但充满生命力的特质。文章更偏向场景报道而非深度乐评，对具体音乐技法的剖析有限，但作为了解中国非主流音乐场景的入口具有参考价值，尤其适合关注亚洲地下实验音乐的听众。

items.body: Review by siLLy puPPy — One of the more adventurous acts to emerge from the small but feisty Portuguese prog scene that hitthe nation like a hurricane after the newfound artistic freedom had emerged after the 1974dictatorial regime collapse with the Carnation Revolution, SAGA was a very short-lived ensemblefronted by songwriter and composer Jos� Lu�s Tinoco and released this one rare obscurity titled HOMOSAPIENS in 1976 on the Movieplay label and pretty much remained completely forgotten until theKorean label M2U reissued it in 2002. This band was somewhat of a supergroup on the Portuguese scenewith a whole slew of prominent Portuguese music industry blokes from jazz, pop and productionuniting for a single no bars hold extravaganza. The band featured multi-instrumentalist Jos� Luis Tinoco as the band's creative force and leader whoplayed piano, synthesizers, keyboards as well as both 6 and 12 string guitars. The band featuredfive additional musicians including Vasco Henriques on Moog and flute, saxophonist R�o Kyao,guitarist and bassist Z� Da Ponte, drummer Fernando Fall� and additional percussionist FernandoGir�o. HOMO SAPIENS was an ambitious concept album tracing human history from the moment of creationall the way to the 20th century and as the album cover art suggests focuses heavily on conflicts andthe horrors of war and fears of nuclear annihilation. The album comes off as a musical and features not only band members on vocal duties which includesgroup sing alongs and narrations in Portuguese but an additional four singers. Sinde Filipe providesdistinct spoken-word narration with vocals by an ensemble featuring Dulce Neves. The music is ratherunique sounding something like fellow countrymen Tantra performing a musical in the style of JesusChrist Superstar. Stylistically HOMO SAPIENS is a complex blend of symphonic prog, jazz fusion(including some Canterbury jazz references) and Portuguese folk and pop with some extraordinarycomplex prog works occurring as well as moments of pure cheesy Euro-pop of the 1970s that was envogue on those talent shows. It's an absolute bizarre labyrinthine approach through the varyingstyles which ranks as one of the most experimental in all of the Portuguese prog scene.The album features 10 tracks at only around 38 minutes which each one very distinct offering a bitof a smorgasbord of ideas much in the vein of the Aphrodite's Child classic "666" which featured asimilar apocalyptic vision in a musical narrative form. Unfortunately for any non-Portuguese speakerthough, this one is completely in the native tongue tailored for the home team made even lessintelligible by the many spoken word narrative passages however even on the musical front, this is ahighly exciting and dynamic journey that conveys the turbulent ups and downs of humanity's journeythroughout the ages. Perhaps a bit over expansive in scope for a mere single album but neverthelesshandled with exquisite care and delivered with excellent performances and passionate vocalistssinging their hearts out.This one comes off as quintessential 70s as this style of musical was all the rage and in that wayit sounds very dated but offers a unique testament to one of the least explored prog scenes in allof 1970s Europe. Sadly the album was a commercial failure upon release despite critical acclaim andhas pretty much remained a distant footnote in the history of 70s prog which is a true shame becausealthough it's not the absolute pinnacle of masterpieces that emerged from the fertile golden years,HOMO SAPIENS is a wild if not bizarre example of creativity in a musical form that wasn't exploredelsewhere as much. This will be one of those that will divide since language is the barrier from anylyrical connection however the musical ingenuity alone is enough to win me over. A nice slice ofrare obscure prog here.

items._cn_summary: 葡萄牙1976年稀有前卫摇滚专辑，以音乐剧形式追溯人类从创世到二十世纪的历史，主题聚焦战争冲突与核毁灭恐惧。作品融合交响前卫、爵士融合、坎特伯雷爵士元素与葡萄牙民间音乐及七十年代欧陆流行曲风，风格跨度极大，被描述为葡萄牙前卫场景中最具实验性的作品之一。乐队阵容类似超级组合，多位葡萄牙爵士、流行与制作领域音乐人参与，运用钢琴、合成器、穆格、萨克斯、长笛等多种乐器，加上群唱、葡萄牙语旁白与四位额外歌手，呈现一部多线索叙事的概念作品。整体虽有非葡萄牙语听众难以完全理解歌词的局限，但在纯音乐层面展现出丰富的动态变化与编曲巧思。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是克劳斯·舒尔茨为电影《Body Love》提交但未被采用的音乐素材，延续了他七十年代柏林学派的电子风格。A面长曲Nowhere占据整张唱片的主要篇幅，呈现出朦胧的合成器氛围，与同时期 Tangerine Dream 营造的声景气质相近，旋律在Moog合成器的缓慢演变中铺陈展开。Stardancer 2作为另一种录制版本出现，缺少鼓手编制，暗示这是一次替代性演绎。终曲Moogetique则以阴郁的音色调制开场，氛围偏向压抑和不安。整体而言，这张专辑与前作相比并无明显突破，舒尔茨将电影配乐中的弃用片段重新整合，并未带来概念或声音设计上的新意。对于熟悉其作品脉络的听众而言，更像是一张补充性记录而非必听之作。

items.body: Review by Sean Trane — Though I've never seen the porno flick, I heard it quite a few times, since laying my ears on it. Don't expect moans & groans, though, but the usual Schulze sonics, if only slightly more exciting than Mirage or X. The opening Stardancer is quite dynamic and could find a spot on a couple of Tangerine Dream albums of the era. Of course, the presence Grosskopf's drums help tremendously. For the life of mine, I can't figure out the anagram of P.T.O., but we're in the Tangerine Dream realm here.I'm still curious how the porno director managed to fit the music to the images, though. I'll probably never find out, though, since a couple of searches for the movie came up empty years ago. In the meantime, I prefer Body Love to Mirage, but giving 4 stars to an OST is relatively rare.
items._cn_summary: 克劳斯·舒尔策为1977年同名成人电影创作的配乐作品，属其早期电子乐探索阶段的代表之一。开篇曲Stardancer动态十足，合成器音色层次丰富，在节奏处理上邀请鼓手Grosskopf参与，使作品比Mirage或X更具活力。整体氛围接近同时期Tangerine Dream的宇宙派电子风格，绵密的音墙与缓慢演变的声景营造出沉浸式听感。乐评者认为此作在OST范畴中相当出色，给予四星评价，并坦言比起Schulze早期作品Mirage更偏爱这张。配乐功能决定其结构需要配合影像，但作为独立聆听依然成立，呈现出七十年代德式电子乐特有的空间感与冥想气质。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Klaus Schulze的第十张录音室作品，以双碟形式呈现，收录六段音乐自传式的长篇器乐曲。评论指出此时期的Schulze已开始重复自我，作品中有少量出色的鼓机段落点缀，但整体缺乏新意。Bayern套曲中邀请的弦乐合奏虽精致却容易令人昏沉，Kleist一曲前半段同样如此，后半段转为略带梦魇感的氛围。评论认为这是Schulze在转向纯氛围与新世纪风格之前的最后一张值得关注的作品，此后其后续作品的集体评分明显下滑。整体属于德国电子/宇宙音乐传统下的渐进式电子作品，与评论者关注的实验电子领域有一定交集。

items.body: The Foreign Resort Endurance Artoffact Records Danish post-punk act The Foreign Resort have never lacked for power nor emotion in their songs. In a live setting, the band have carefully walked the line between stormy, thrashing grooves and the more angular edges of their material, and yet their preceding albums have been inconsistent in capturing the force of their performances. New record Endurance arrives a full seven years since the release of preceding LP Outnumbered, and finds the trio at both their tightest and most reflective, addressing personal and political strife with a focus that pushes through the uncertainty and angst with bracing determination. Part of the record’s appeal is certainly in how it charges headlong into extremely personal and relatable emotional territory, heart on its sleeve and with complete and total sincerity. Early album cut “Resound”, amongst the best songs they’ve ever recorded, epitomizes this approach; it bursts out of the gate, vocalist Mikkel Borbjerg Jakobsen working his quavering Robert Smith-esque lilt atop a galloping bass groove and wiry guitars, the implied heartache of the verse washed away by the conviction and feeling of its chorus. While not always that fraught, the record returns to that emotional well repeatedly, and squeezes the most out of it each time. As its titles suggests, “Closure” contrasts the melancholy of finality with the release of being able to move on with your life, while the speedy, yelping “Southern Skies” taps into classic out-of-the-blue-into-the-black rock sentiment with rare commitment. It’s invigorating no doubt, and works because the band is so good at building up the sentimental core of each song before providing a cathartic release. Opener “Despair” takes its time building a depressive and anxious portrait of isolation in the modern world, slowly building from the sparse and atmospheric verses to an underplayed and sincere message of connection, its cloudy pads blown away by cleansing swells of shoegaze distortion. Similarly, the title track uses space and thin, muscly bass and synth programming to create a tension commensurate with its theme of societal and political instability, the stridency of its refrain and that implores us to stand together and hold on seeming all the more resolute for the time spent getting there. Endurance is certainly the best The Foreign Resort have ever sounded on a record, both in terms of the strength of the songs, and in the resolve and the earnestness they embody. It’s a record of sturm and drang, the tumult matched by its insistence that the answer is not to retreat from the darkness, but to reaffirm our connections, to each other and the world at large. Recommended. Buy it. Endurance by The Foreign Resort The post The Foreign Resort, “Endurance” appeared first on I Die: You Die.
items._cn_summary: 丹麦后朋克乐队The Foreign Resort暌违七年推出新专辑，由独立厂牌Artoffact Records发行。整张专辑在情感表达上极为真诚直接，歌词聚焦个人困境与社会政治动荡，旋律层面则从阴沉压抑的氛围逐渐推进到释放与救赎。开篇曲Despair以稀疏的合成器铺垫搭建出孤独图景，随后被自赏式吉他音墙冲散；同名曲Endurance利用大段留白与紧绷的低音线及合成器节奏制造张力，呼应其关于社会动荡的主题。Resound展现出主唱近似Robert Smith的颤抖声线，搭配奔腾的贝斯与棱角分明的吉他，哀愁的副歌被坚定信念所替代。乐队在构建歌曲情感内核后给予宣泄式释放的编曲逻辑贯穿全作，使专辑在情绪强度与音乐执行层面都达到乐队生涯最佳水准。

items.body: With Cold Cause, we welcome a Franco-German trio releasing their debut album on the renowned Manic Depression Records. The album presents nine tracks that immediately reveal influences from bands such as Lebanon Hanover. What unfolds is a minimalist Electro-Wave sound in which icy synthesizers and guitar lines merge into a dark and atmospheric landscape, all driven by compelling, danceable rhythms. The female vocals, delivered in both German and English, possess a cold, detached quality that perfectly suits this style of music while remaining utterly captivating. Several tracks stand out through their strong dancefloor appeal, adding an extra layer of energy and intensity to the album. The combination of haunting melodies, restrained arrangements, and infectious rhythms creates a sound that feels both familiar and refreshing. This is a highly successful debut from a band that already has the potential to secure a prominent place within the genre. (Rating:8). Listen to “Dead Diamond Machine”: https://coldcause.bandcamp.com/track/dead-diamond-machine
items._cn_summary: Cold Cause 是法德三人组合的首张专辑，由 Manic Depression Records 发行，共收录九首作品。整体呈现出极简主义电子浪潮风格，冰冷的合成器音色与吉他线条交织，营造出阴暗而富有氛围感的声景，节奏部分具备强烈的舞池感与可舞性。女声主唱以德语和英语交替演唱，冷淡疏离的处理方式与音乐气质高度契合。专辑在编排上偏于克制，旋律带有一定的回响感与记忆点，多首曲目在舞曲张力上表现突出。乐评将其与 Lebanon Hanover 相提并论，指出作品在熟悉类型语汇的基础上保持了新鲜感。作为一张首张专辑，展现了该组合在暗潮领域的潜力与方向，整体完成度较高，但在声音设计的独创性与实验维度上仍有拓展空间。

items._cn_summary: 这是一篇关于Dave Burrell 1969年专辑《Echo》的唱片信息整理，内容以Discogs式的发行资料为主，缺少实质性乐评。专辑由BYG Records发行，属于法国Actuel系列自由爵士代表作之一，1969年8月13日在巴黎录制，仅含两首长篇作品：《Echo》(20:02)与《Peace》(21:30)。阵容汇集了自由爵士场景的多位重要乐手：钢琴兼作曲者Dave Burrell领衔，萨克斯方面有Archie Shepp（次中音）和Arthur Jones（中音），小号手Clifford Thornton，长号手Grachan Moncur III，贝斯Alan Silva，鼓手Sunny Murray。整张专辑呈现典型的60年代末纽约—巴黎自由爵士迁徙路线，即兴对话密集、结构自由展开，是了解欧洲前卫爵士厂牌BYG的关键文献之一。

items._cn_summary: 这是1969年由法国小厂牌BYG Actuel发行的自由爵士唱片，标题虽印作Way Head，正确名称应为Way Ahead。录音于巴黎Saravah工作室完成，阵容包括小号手Jacques Coursil、中音萨克斯Arthur Jones、低音提琴Beb Guérin与鼓手Claude Delcloo，仅三首曲目，分别为7分35秒的Duke、10分03秒的Fidel以及长达18分45秒的Paper，给予乐手充分的即兴延展空间。该专辑归属BYG的Actuel系列，是欧洲自由爵士厂牌中深具实验色彩的分支，Coursil承担全部编曲。原文基本为唱片资料罗列，缺乏实际乐评与听感描述。

items.body:
A properly delectable suite of sexy, downbeat dream-pop returns on 3rd pressing with its maker, Kai Hugo’s Antwerp-based World of Paint, acutely tipped to those who missed the 2020 + 2021 editions, and anyone who holds a flame for Johnny Jewel, Julee Cruise, Dirty Beaches

Back by demand - 2nd hand copies are known to trade for triple figures - ‘I’m Cindy’ is a chef’s kiss of effortlessly slow, seductive lo-fi songwriting that practically smushes earlobes with its heavenly marriage of Kai Hugo, aka Palmbomen’s faded production lustre and singer, Blue LoLãn’s range of whispered sweet nothings and harmonised coo. In the years since its original release it’s taken on a life of its own as a go-to succour for lovers of blissed-out, cinematic waft with equal measures of soft-focus, nostalgic FM synth gauze and details that caress, crack in all the right, tender places. 

Conceptually derived from Palmbomen II’s ‘Memories of Cindy’ session of 2017, the 13 tracks find marbled whorls of sensual fascination within that LP’s fantasy reminiscence, here expanded into a spectrum of LA-via-Antwerp dream-pop like Johnny Jewel meets Alex Zhang Hungtai on the synth and sax pearl ‘Another’ or lip-smacking cruiser ‘Justin’, thru a Voice Actor-esque ‘Voice Message’ and the gossamer FM synth fronds that wrap it up on ‘Maybe Because It’s Over Now’, whilst secreting shimmers of Vince Clarke ballads in ‘2y & 6m’, and acid-laced lo-fi machine crack shades away from Maria Minerva on ’Never Let Me Go’.

No brainer!
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是比利时安特卫普制作人Kai Hugo（化名Palmbomen）联手歌手Blue LoLãn打造的梦幻流行作品，源自其2017年项目《Memories of Cindy》的概念延伸。十三首曲目以缓慢、性感的低保真合成器为底色，融合FM合成器的朦胧纱感、复古萨克斯点缀和简约电子节拍，营造出洛杉矶与安特卫普之间飘渺的怀旧氛围。制作上强调模拟质感的褪色光泽，人声以低语哼唱和和声叠加为主，与Johnny Jewel、Julee Cruise等暗潮梦幻系艺人的美学血脉相近。整体编排偏向氛围化与电影感，虽非激进实验，但在合成器音色设计和情绪铺陈上展现出细腻的品味与独到审美。

items.body:
‘Aftersun’ composer Coates furnishes a score of heart-in-mouth classical strings, keys and choral arrangements to gay romance flick ‘Pillion’, aka an opportunity to ogle Alexander Skarsgård, replete with biker leathers, in a sub-dom relationship

By now one of the preeminent composers in his field - up there with Mica Levi, 0PN, Bobby Krlic et al - Coates continues to expand and hone his distinctly classic yet fresh palette and chops to purpose on this particularly lush set of orchestrations and sweeping sound design, including his take on a Satie evergreen. Gently gelled to the film’s narrative, revolving a shy yung queer lad seduced into a BDSM relationship with a dashing local biker, Coates’ score is ravishingly sensual and heady, full of oneiric allusions to classical, ambient, lavish ballads and twinkling electronica, all sure to hit pleasure centres of anyone who fancies Romance, Jonny Greenwood’s ‘Phantom Thread’ OST, Enya’s crushed velvet wafters, or event schmaltziest ends of Leyland Kirby.
items._cn_summary: Oliver Coates 为电影《Pillion》创作的配乐延续了他在《Aftersun》中的古典弦乐与键盘语汇，融合了合唱编排和氛围化的电子音效处理，乐评将其与 Mica Levi、Jonny Greenwood 并提，暗示其当代古典配乐中的实验倾向。作品中包含对 Satie 经典曲目的重新演绎，整体呈现出梦幻、感官化的质感。乐评特别强调其声音设计的精致度以及对电影叙事的贴合：音乐服务于一个关于羞怯年轻人被引入 BDSM 关系的同性恋浪漫故事，暗示其中可能包含暗黑、亲密的氛围层次。配乐跨界于古典、室内乐、氛围音乐和微妙的电子元素之间，对偏好当代古典与实验融合的听众有吸引力，但本质上仍是服务于影像的电影配乐作品。

items.body:
Alt Dub label head Federsen links with Belgrade’s Estray for a deep, percussive exploration of dub house.

"A key figure within Eastern Europe’s electronic landscape, Estray has spent over a decade shaping a sound that travels far beyond his home base. With releases on Rebellion, Neptune Discs, Sol Selectas, Akumandra and Buddha Bar, alongside an extensive international DJ presence, his output reflects a balance of cultural depth and dancefloor functionality.

His productions draw on a wide palette of influences, fusing African and Latin rhythmic structures with rolling, dub-informed low-end. Intricate drum programming and fluid groove design sit at the core, while his basslines—heavy, warm and propulsive—remain a defining signature. Federsen, known for releases on Echospace Detroit, Grayscale, Synchrophone, Lempuyang and Avant Roots, continues to refine a sound rooted in analogue process, spatial detail and textural precision. His work leans into restraint, allowing depth and subtle modulation to drive momentum.

Recorded at Devon Analogue Studios, the pair’s collaboration unfolds across four tracks built on dense sub frequencies, shifting percussion and evolving atmospheres. Each piece is carefully structured yet organic, moving between stripped-back dub frameworks and more rhythmically charged passages.

The result is a cohesive body of work that sits comfortably within the dub house tradition while introducing a broader, multicultural rhythmic language—equally suited to immersive listening and deep dancefloor moments."
items._genre: dub house / electronic / deep dub / percussive
items._cn_summary: 这是一张在德文模拟录音室完成的四曲合作EP，Estray与Federsen各自拥有东欧和英国地下电子场景的深厚背景。作品以低频sub为基底，融合非洲与拉丁节奏结构与dub低音线，在繁复的鼓组编程与流畅律动之间取得平衡。整体走向介于极简dub骨架与节奏密度较高的段落之间，注重空间纵深、模拟质感与细微调制对动态的推动力。作为dub house领域的作品，它融入了多元文化节奏语言，兼具沉浸聆听与舞池实用两种取向，对电子音乐爱好者尤其是dub house及deep techno方向的听众具有参考价值。

items.body:
Prolific Canadians Priori & Project Pablo, aka Jump Source, refract fine strains of deep house, indie-pop, dub and techno-pop on an expansive LP ft. guest vox by billy woods, CFCF & Loukeman and advised to admirers of Luomo, Nick Léon, Rosa Terenzi & D. Tiffany, Galcher Lustwerk.

Building on a decade of Jump Source 12”s for Pacific Rhythm and their self-titled label, Francis Latreille & Patrick Holland skip to the former’s mothership, NAFF, for the project’s variegated debut album. The range and subtle recombinant steez of ‘Fold’ plays deep into the duo’s role at the core of Canada’s renowned club sound, which has emerged over the past decade with canniest updates and refinements of ‘90s to ‘00s US, UK x EU house, techno, trance and beyond. All the above can be heard stripped for parts and reassembled according to classic club lust and galvanised with slick production sure to see it gather air miles.

Tune to tune they fine-tune nuanced aspects of style and pattern, from tweaked darkroom electro-house with over-the-shoulder vox in ‘Nice & Edgy’ calling to mind Cheap & Deep Productions, to the pearlescent ambient-pop of ‘Close’ ft. POiSON GiRL FRiEND. Standouts are registered in the deep house of ‘Empty Bars’ that finds cult rapper billy woods out of context on a groove co-produced with Nick Léon, and in the echoes of Canadian click-house pioneer Akufen on ‘Affect’ ft. Loukeman, thru the brisker deep techno-house of ‘Fade City’ ft. Deaton Chris Anthony, and the Luomo-esque, connoisseurs choice of ‘A Dull Knife’ faced by Harmony Index.
items._cn_summary: 加拿大双人组Jump Source的首张全长专辑将深层浩室、独立流行、dub与techno-pop等多种风格拆解重组，展现出对九十至两千年代欧美俱乐部音乐语汇的精细化更新。制作上注重纹理层次与风格细节的微调，从暗室电气到珍珠光泽的氛围流行，每首曲目都聚焦于不同声音维度的探索。客串阵容包括地下说唱歌手billy woods、Nick Léon、CFCF等人，为以浩室为骨架的作品注入跨语境的质感与声线层次。整体定位偏向细腻精致的俱乐部聆听体验，融合多位客座带来的声景变化，在浩室传统的框架内进行分子级的拆解与重铸，适合偏好精致电子声响、关注俱乐部文化深层脉络的听者。

items.body:
Part 2 of a 12" series featuring Beatrice M.’s 'Sinking', the rudely aerodynamic debut LP where Tectonic's franco-british hope flexes a signature balance of ruff & smooth, building on a solid reputation earned via 12”s with her label, Bait, plus Tempa and Darwin’s SPE:C.

Dubstep is not necessarily an album genre: beyond scant examples from the likes of Burial, Shackleton, or 2562, 12”s and DJ sets serve the sound in best context. However, Beatrice M.’s grasp of subtle sensuality and propulsive traction patently ends itself well to the format on ’Sinking’, with rolling, stepping and skanking permutations that deftly dance in the space between dubstep, proper, and its close-related cousins - UKG, broken beat, dub techno - with a finely measured proprioception of space, weight and pressure. 

Along with 2562’s recently dispensed ‘Lost Dubs 2006-09’, ’Sinking’ is arguably the best thing on Tectonic in recent memory, with a sound that revels in more ambiguous club suss. It’s the type of release primed for cans/buds as much as big cones, proving she’s equally adept at sublime tension, as in the weightless love note ‘Dear Dubstep’, and thru the 2562-like fluid hydrodynamics of ‘Juice.’.
items._genre: dubstep / UKG / broken beat / dub techno
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Beatrice M.的首张全长作品，收录于Tectonic厂牌，以12寸单曲形式分批发行。乐评指出她的音乐在dubstep、UKG、broken beat与dub techno之间游走，展现出对空间、重量与压力的细腻控制力。专辑既包含轻盈抒情的'Dear Dubstep'，也有如'Juice'般充满流体动力学感的2562式律动，兼具耳机的私密聆听与大型音响系统的舞池冲击力。乐评将其与2562的近期作品并列为Tectonic近年最佳，强调其在模糊俱乐部音乐与精致制作之间取得的平衡。对于偏好实验与电子交叉领域的听众而言，这是一种值得关注的声音探索，但整体仍扎根于dubstep舞曲传统，实验性更多体现在质感层面而非结构突破。

items.body: Smileswithteeth takes some chances on this self-titled album, but not before reminding us of the reasons we’ve been following the artist for thirteen years. Yes, the career of Gabriel Gutierrez has now become a teenager! Smileswithteeth has been solid since the start, when Here established a template of warm beats and electronics. This year, the artist spreads his wings. We start in “19999.” No, that’s not a typo. Electronics churn like a changing radio dial, waiting to settle on a song. And soon they do, with the album’s first single, “Radio Feel Better,” a disco rhythm emerging from the shadows of the old century to inject itself into the new. There’s a bit of Daft Punk in these grooves, giving the electro-leaning track a real shot at crossover success: a summer classic in the making. As a child says, “Make me feel better like you always do,” we recall the child of “Roomies;” Gutierrez has always exuded a sense of childlike innocence. “vocstl” is a change of pace, set in the center of the album: an ambient piece characterized by lapping waves and bubbling synth. Later in the set, “ILU” will continue this thread, embedding dialogue in a buttery dish. The water itself returns in the middle of “川” as the rush of a wave bisects the percussive instrumental, and again in the second minute of “Black Sea.” There is some singing on the album, buried at first in the humble vocals of “So Clear.” ~trinity~ appears on “Running Out of Time,” which recalls indietronica, proceeding from beeps ‘n’ beats to rapid percussion and stuttering lines. “I Could Never” offers a brush of guitars, foreshadowing things to come. On “POV,” Smileswithteeth channels Postal Service, a duo that existed only for a halcyon moment. The left turn occurs in “Bleeding Out in the Valley,” an all-out rock tune with distorted guitars and a lo-fi vibe; it seems beamed in from another universe. As much as we like the track on its own, it doesn’t fit the timbre of its neighbors, while the timbre of the subsequent “Black Sea” does, and the closing “HFMB” successfully combines both influences. Smileswithteeth is branching out, as teenagers are wont to do: experimenting with different styles, flirting with radio success. But at the same time, Smileswithteeth is a radio fan, continuing to turn the dial to the left and right, searching for foreign frequencies in late-night grooves. To lose a tooth at the age of the child on the cover is to anticipate a new tooth, and on Smileswithteeth we can hear this tooth growing. Smileswithteeth seems poised for a breakthrough; the only question is, “pop or electronic?” (Richard Allen)
items._genre: indietronica / electronic / ambient pop / lo-fi rock
items._cn_summary: Smileswithteeth 的同名专辑是艺术家 Gutierrez 十三年来的一次转折点。整张专辑以电子为骨架，融合迪斯科律动、环境声景与独立电子元素，开篇的电子信号如同调拨收音机频道，从嘈杂中浮现第一支单曲的舞曲节奏，带有 Daft Punk 式的复古质感。专辑中段以水流声、泡泡合成器构建的氛围段落呈现实验性的一面，而"Bleeding Out in the Valley"突然转向失真吉他与低保真摇滚，与整体电子氛围产生明显断裂。词曲人声被刻意埋藏在混音底层，呼应艺术家一贯的童真主题。专辑展现了从纯电子到摇滚的跨度尝试，独立小厂牌发行避免了商业化嫌疑，对追求跨界融合的听众有一定吸引力，但整体仍偏向主流可听性而非深度实验。

items.body: Fly the ocean on this silver plane of an album. It’s a smooth flight full of gentle transitions, giving a contemplative view of the larger landscape of our lives. Astral realms of buttery, finger picked, electric softness Fly the Ocean in a Silver Plane by Pan•American   There is nothing to get cranky about when the tinkling electronics and gentle guitar shimmer of Pan•American begin their ascent into cloud lined realms. Mark Nelson has been on a prolific streak, having made two albums with Kramer in 2024 and 2025, another album with Michael Grigoni in 2025. His last solo extended solo outing was the Alpalhão EP in 2022 and now he returns with a full-length record of his own. For this record he takes the imagery of the airplane into astral realms of buttery, finger picked, electric softness. Gentle notes ride on the buoyance of air, and resonate with impressionistic stratocumulus puffs of breezy synth pads and the slow warmth of languid syncopation.As the album unfolds it goes from being guitar forward with electronics, to electronica forward with less and less guitar at its apogee, and then moves back in the other direction again. It seems that the higher the plane ascends into the sky realms, the less tethered the music is to the traditional instrumentation and the more fully it embraces the electronic. Then it comes back to being more guitar forward, the plane descending back down to the runway. The tones conjured out of these high-strung strings relieve tension through emotive ambient fretwork. Perhaps the gradual transition represents the way the soul sheds the body as it transitions into death. It wouldn’t be surprising, because that is one of the themes on this Pan•American outing. Of my varied interests, dreams and their interpretation have been a continuous area of fascination. Dreams of airports and airplanes have often presaged the death of a loved one, or been places where the dead come back to commune with the living. Airplanes and airports are liminal zones. As Nelson writes in his notes on the album, “Having experienced the arrival of my children, the decline and departure of my parents, and the many years of venturing out and returning home in my own life, travel feels like the perfect tropology to consider the mysteries we inhabit.” The afterlife theme :: The afterlife theme is reflected in the song titles such as, “Death Cleaning,” “Entrance to Afterlife,” “Heaven’s Waiting Room,” “Taxi to the Terminal Gate,” and “Golden Gate, Silver City.” Nelson uses two songs to create what he calls “the spine of this music.” One is “You Belong to Me” by Jo Stafford and the other is Chuck Berry’s “Promised Land.” Using material from these he is able to further embellish his sound paintings with notions of loneliness from theone left behind from the Stafford song, with the hopeful Americana of the freedom to move and travel that Berry’s tune about going to California in the time of segregation. Here we hear another aspect of the United States as we did on his album New World, Lonely Ride with Grigoni, but hear from the comfort of a Silver Plane traveling at cruising altitudes. The recurrence of these themes is probably to be expected as there was overlap in his recording of this while making the string of other albums mentioned above. This album sounds very personal and reflective. The cover shows a photo of his mother that he did not know or see until after her passing. “With the headscarf and that excited, nervous expression, she looks about to embark on a journey. Ready, finally, to cross the tarmac and board the Silver Plane.” Fly the ocean on this silver plane of an album. It’s a smooth flight full of gentle transitions, giving a contemplative view of the larger landscape of our lives. Fly the Ocean in a Silver Plane is available on Kranky. items._cn_summary: Pan•American（Mark Nelson 的个人计划）在 Kranky 厂牌发行了这张以飞行旅程为隐喻的专辑。整体音乐风格从吉他主导的民谣质感逐渐过渡为电子主导的氛围化声响，再回归吉他结构，模拟飞机起降的弧线。指弹吉他与闪烁的合成器音色构成松弛的纹理，缓慢的切分节奏带来冥想式温度。歌曲标题如"死后清理""天堂候机室"等指向来世与离别主题，Nelson 以 Jo Stafford 和 Chuck Berry 的经典旋律作为情感骨架，将怀旧与解放交织。专辑探讨旅行作为人生过渡的象征性，介于具象器乐与抽象电子之间的渐变过程是核心手法。

items.body: Los Tre have been playing instrumental music in Athens since 2012, when guitarist Angelos Angelides, bassist Vassilis Papastamopoulos and drummer Leandros Fratnik set up as a jazz-funk trio in the middle of Greece’s debt crisis. “A Kala” comes from their sixth album, Taha Mu, by which point the band had grown into a quartet with percussionist Angelos Polychronou and pushed well past jazz-funk: electric and loose, built on grooves pulled from West Africa, Ethiopia and Greece, the guitar run through heavy fuzz. The record was cut at Fabliquid Studio in early 2024 and mixed by Paul Stefanidis. Improvisation runs through everything they do, on record and on the Athens stages where they’ve built their name. items._cn_summary: 希腊雅典乐团LOS TRE自2012年成立，最初为三人爵士放克编制，在希腊债务危机背景下起步。这首《A Kala》出自其第六张专辑Taha Mu，经过十余年发展，乐队已扩展为四人阵容，加入打击乐手，风格也从爵士放克拓展至更宽广的领域。音乐以律动为核心，融合西非、埃塞俄比亚与希腊传统元素，吉他经过重失真处理，整体呈现电气化、松弛而流动的声音质感。整张专辑在Fabliquid Studio录制，于2024年初完成混音，即兴演奏贯穿所有作品。乐评指出乐队在雅典现场积累了相当声誉，其创作方式兼具录音室精细与现场即兴的自由度，是一支扎根地中海东部的跨文化融合力量。

items.body: Those of us who have been digging into Analog Africa�s increasingly formidable releases over the last two decades are well aware of the massive amount of raw, vodun-based Sato and Sakpata-derived funk the label has issued by Benin�s most prolific 1970s-era band, the Orchestre Poly-Ritmo. AA has dropped no fewer than 3 compilations of their heaviest material, as well as a reissue of the band�s first LP, in an effort to give them the international status they deserve. That being said, what might be different about this collection of their music? And who is Antoine Dougb�? Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa As it turns out, Dougb� was a song-conjurer whose mode of musical transfer was slapping his legs in a rhythm known as Cavacha, a groove created by drummer Belobi Meridjo, who was inspired by a train cadence that he worked into a pattern that ultimately spread like a 21st century California wildfire throughout Congolese pop music in the mid-1970s. Dougb�, known as the �Devil�s Prime Minister,� was also a practitioner of vodun who inspired fear in any musician he felt was unsuited to play his music, which is how he landed on working exclusively Poly-Ritmo, as he felt they could nail what he wanted in ways other bands couldn�t. His recording career was brief - 3 albums and a few singles - but as this collection shows, it was potent. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa Because of the era from which this music dates, it�s not surprising that the recording and instrument tones have changed - the guitars have a plastic sheen and synthesizers appear- even if the music remains rooted in the 1970s. Perhaps the influence of the Cuban son is more apparent here than on other Poly-Ritmo collections, especially in the collection�s initial offerings. And yes, Congolese rumba, then shaking all of sub-Saharan Africa to its knees, is present too. �Ma Won Min Towe Leo� is one example. Opening with a bed of synthesizers, the shimmering guitars, tinny, seemingly squeezed dry by the 80s themselves, lock in over relentless high-hat-focused grooves. The guitars finally start firing in different directions midway through, before that synth weaves back in, forming a bed underneath it all. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa �We Tayi Sin Assi Tche� is much more overtly Cuban. With its insistent cowbell, classic, nasal vocal call and response, and tight, repeated guitar figures, its debt to mid-twentieth century Afro-Cuban sons is transparent. Another track, �Djomido Ma Dougbe Tche� rides a groove reminiscent of 70�s-era Franco classic �Liberte.� The pulse is relentless, and the guitar solo repeats a tight repetition of a few notes, driving listeners to ecstasy all the while. However, none of this music is a mere copy of its influences; rather, like so much potent pop coming from the continent at the time, it is a swirl of major influences rendered by local rhythms and vocal phrasing to give it specific identity, in this case, to Benin. Dougb�s musical role on this collection is a bit murky. One of his three albums has a photo of him, fully mic�d behind a collection of hand drums, so perhaps he served as a percussionist/vocalist; this release never explains. He wasn�t a songwriter in the traditional sense. It seems he was more of an instigator and arranger, but his thumbprint was apparently heavy enough to warrant his name on the records he was involved with. Whatever the case, in his brief run as a recording artist, he and Poly-Ritmo produced a handful of driving, Cavacha-inspired grooves that can still wear holes in club floors. Further reading: Petrona Mart�nez - Ancestras (Review) Gnonnas Pedro & His Dadjes - Roi De L'Agbadja Moderne 1974-1983 (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑聚焦贝宁传奇乐团Orchestre Poly-Rythmo与词曲创作者Antoine Dougbé在1977至1982年间的合作录音。Dougbé以拍腿节奏Cavacha闻名，这一律动源自鼓手Belobi Meridjo对火车节奏的提炼，后广泛影响1970年代中期的刚果流行乐。评论指出这批录音相比该乐团此前发行物更明显地吸收了古巴son元素，尤其在开篇曲目中可辨，持续的康加鼓型与鼻音唱腔构成典型古巴对唱结构；同时也融入了席卷撒哈拉以南非洲的刚果伦巴。录音时代特征突出——吉他带有塑料质感光泽、合成器开始进入编制，但整体仍扎根于七十年代节奏框架。Analog Africa作为挖掘非洲冷门律动的独立厂牌，此为其第44号发行，已是该乐团第三或第四次系统整理。

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由吉他手兼音乐文献学者Dominique Cravic与Les Primitifs du futur乐队录制，是一张风格无法归类的作品。乐队在27首短曲中融合了法国bal-musette、拉格泰姆、jug band、法国香颂乃至skiffle等多种早期流行音乐传统，使用手风琴、萨克斯、木琴、单簧管、班卓琴、尤克里里、特雷门琴、夏威夷吉他、风笛及音乐锯等大量复古乐器。Cravic的演唱方式类似平民化的Maurice Chevalier，以talk-sing的方式呈现。专辑选曲包括1925年的《Ukulele Lady》，以及向2020年去世的法国抵抗运动女歌手Juliette Gréco致敬的《N'oublie pas Gréco》，并以法语翻唱《Smoke Gets in Your Eyes》《Take Five》《As Time Goes By》等经典。乐队成员大多年过七旬，Cravic形容自己说：'年轻人有火焰，但我们有光'。专辑体现了对被遗忘音乐传统的严肃挖掘与重新演绎。

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."
items._genre: field recording / spoken word / documentary / sound art
items._cn_summary: 这是一张来自芝加哥南区的田野录音作品，由录音师Ian Brennan策划录制，二十五位枪支暴力幸存者在社区前廊讲述自身经历。编辑直言这并非传统意义上的音乐，仅含少量即兴说唱。文章不是标准乐评，而是放弃评论让原始录音与录音师短评自行发声。文章着重呈现暴力对社区的全面渗透——参与者年龄从十七到六十七岁，几乎无人幸免。一位老人在讲述失去两个儿子后反复道歉，而编辑指出该道歉的对象应是社会本身。录音录制当天恰逢特朗普下令向该市部署国民警卫队，地点位于米德韦机场降落航道正下方。文章将收益捐给反暴力组织Cure Violence Global。录音完全由现场环境声构成，无任何后期音乐叠加，是一份具有社会纪实价值的声学文献。

items.body:
In 2026, I was invited to join the Silkroad Ensemble, the international collective directed by Rhiannon Giddens, as a musician (frame drums, violin, and voice) and contributor of new arrangements and compositions. Following an initial workshop and preview performance in New York in January 2026, the project will unfold through a North American tour in March 2026, featuring nine concerts alongside workshops and community outreach activities across the United States, as part of the new program
Sanctuary: The Power of Resonance and Ritual
. The tour will continue later in the year with further residencies and performances in North America and Europe.
There are musical projects that are built around a repertoire, others around a geography, and others still around a specific aesthetic vision. The Silkroad Ensemble belongs to a different category: it is a living organism built around an idea. A simple and radical idea at once�that music can be a real space of encounter between cultures, not as a symbolic gesture, but as a daily, concrete, lived practice.
Founded in 1998 by Yo-Yo Ma, Silkroad has never been an ensemble in the traditional sense. There is no fixed lineup, no stable repertoire. Instead, it is a community of musicians from different traditions, chosen not only for their technical excellence, but for their ability to inhabit a threshold�the space between rootedness and transformation. Each musician brings with them a language, a sound, a memory. What matters most is the willingness to place that language in dialogue with others, without hierarchy.
In recent years, the project has been guided by Rhiannon Giddens, one of the most powerful and deeply insightful voices in contemporary music. Her presence gives the work a clear direction: the goal is not to create an artificial synthesis of traditions, but to create the conditions for each tradition to speak fully, and to transform through encounter. Rhiannon possesses a rare kind of leadership�one that never imposes itself, but quietly shapes the space, both musically and humanly.
Entering this context means immediately finding yourself in a space where musical identity is not something to defend, but something to offer. The pizzica, the frame drums, the violin I carry with me are no longer only instruments of a local tradition, but elements in a broader conversation, where every sound is heard both for what it is and for what it might become.
It is within this space that my participation in Sanctuary: The Power of Resonance and Ritual began to take shape. Even before the music itself, what stands out is the quality of listening. A real, deep listening, in which every musical gesture is at once personal and collective. This, perhaps, is the true nature of Silkroad: not simply an ensemble, but a place. A circle. A space where music returns to what it has always been�a form of relationship.
Sanctuary: The Power of Resonance and Ritual
Music as Refuge and Resistance
The word sanctuary can be understood in many ways: refuge, protected space, a place where it is still possible to pause, to listen, to rebuild a sense of community.
Working on this project in the United States today carries a particular weight. This is a country marked by deep and increasingly visible tensions, where public discourse is often shaped by fear, by closure, by the idea that identity is something to be defended against someone else. The same tendency can be seen elsewhere�in Italy, across Europe, and in many parts of the world. The rise of nationalism, ongoing wars, and increasingly restrictive migration policies contribute to a climate in which separation begins to feel like the natural order of things.
Within this context, finding yourself in a room each day with musicians from Morocco, India, Japan, Armenia, Scotland, Congo, Italy, and the United States becomes something very real. Each person brings their own history, their own sound, their own way of inhabiting music. What emerges is not a fusion of identities, but their coexistence.
The taranta, Gnawa music, Indian classical tradition, American folk music�these practices were never conceived merely as forms of entertainment. They were born as tools to accompany moments of transformation, to help individuals and communities move through crisis, grief, healing, and renewal.
Sanctuary begins with this understanding. With the idea that music can still be a space where encounter is possible without the need to simplify or protect oneself. A space where listening becomes an act of trust.
Something simple and real happens: people from different parts of the world breathe together, listen together, and build something that did not exist before. In a time that often pushes toward division, this act acquires a different weight. It becomes, in its own quiet way, a form of resistance.
Entering the Circle
The first rehearsals are always a delicate moment. I took part in an initial workshop in Ireland last December, with a smaller group�Rhiannon, Mazz, Francesco, Niwel, and myself�and then a second workshop with the full ensemble in January, followed by a beautiful preview performance in New York on January 10, 2026, as part of the Winter Jazz Fest.
At that stage, there is no shared language yet. You observe each other, you play, you try things, you listen. What strikes you immediately is the extraordinary musical and human level of the people involved. They are incredible. Not only great instrumentalists, but musicians who have developed a deep relationship with their own musical traditions, and who have learned to question them, to keep them flexible and alive.
The Hawaiian bassist Shawn Conley, for example, moves effortlessly between bow and pizzicato, shifting from a lyrical, singing tone to remarkable rhythmic agility, using the instrument with a freedom that easily recalls the expressive range of a cello.
Beside him, Scottish harpist Maeve Gilchrist brings a presence that is both refined and fearless. Beyond a complete mastery of everything one might expect from the harp�the luminous, almost celestial sound�she possesses an extraordinary rhythmic and harmonic awareness, and a musical curiosity that allows her to make bold, unexpected choices without hesitation.
Armenian cellist Karen Ouzounian represents the very highest level of classical tradition, but with something more: a strong personal voice, a deep compositional sensibility, and a lyrical approach to improvisation that makes every gesture feel necessary.
With Francesco Turrisi, who like me comes from Italy, we already share a longer history. Yet I remain constantly struck by his ability to move between radically different instruments�accordion, piano, frame drums, string instruments�with complete naturalness. His immense musicality is not tied to any single instrument, but to a broader understanding of sound, form, and structure.
Congolese guitarist Niwel Tsumbu is simply one of the finest guitarists I have ever encountered. His relationship with the guitar transcends the instrument itself. He brings together a deep knowledge of African musical traditions, an innate rhythmic sensibility, refined harmonic awareness, and an extraordinary improvisational freedom.
Kaoru Watanabe embodies, in a profound way, the idea that tradition is also a choice. Japanese and American, he moves fluidly between cultural languages with a rare balance of respect, discipline, and expressive freedom. His playing is never a reproduction of the past, but its living continuation.
With Mehdi Nassouli, on guembri and voice, I feel a particular closeness. Like me with pizzica, he belongs deeply to a specific musical world�in his case, the Gnawa tradition of Morocco. Yet his experience has given him an equally deep ability to engage in dialogue with other musical languages, without ever losing the center of his own sound.
Sandeep Das�s presence on tabla is a constant point of reference. He is, quite literally, a guru of Indian music, and yet his authority never creates distance. On the contrary, he makes every interaction feel natural, effortless, both musically and humanly.
Japanese percussionist Haruka Fujii brings an extraordinary level of precision and listening. Her virtuosity is never displayed for its own sake, but always placed in service of the music, strengthening the cohesion of the ensemble.
American violinist and vocalist Mazz Swift embodies a rare combination of strength and openness. Their voice and violin move fluidly across genres and traditions, grounded yet constantly searching, expanding the expressive space of the group.
And then there is Rhiannon. It is difficult to find a single word that captures her presence. She is a complete musician�singer, instrumentalist, composer, dancer, and leader�but above all, she possesses a clarity of vision that holds everything together and inspires everyone around her. Her leadership does not operate through control, but through listening. She creates a space in which each musician can fully express themselves, while contributing to something larger than any individual voice.
Common Ground
"Common Ground" is the pizzica I wrote for the Silkroad Ensemble. I use the word �wrote� with caution, because the piece truly exists only through the creative contribution of each musician involved. I laid the foundations: the rhythm, the groove, the structure, the overall architecture, and the fixed melodic and harmonic elements. But what makes it alive is the way each musician inhabits it.
The idea first emerged during the workshop in Ireland. At that stage, we were still searching for common ground, a way of being together musically without renouncing our individual identities. It felt natural for me to bring the rhythm of pizzica�my familiar and chosen refuge, my Sanctuary.
Back home, I began to develop that intuition, shaping a structure that preserved the physical and rhythmic core of the tradition, while remaining open enough to allow each musician to find their own place within it. We worked on the piece during the workshop in the United States, and performed it live for the first time in New York, just days later, at the Winter Jazz Fest.
It was extraordinary to witness how naturally each musician entered that rhythm without hesitation. No one was trying to imitate something that did not belong to them. Instead, each voice emerged clearly, freely coexisting alongside the others.
In that moment, I understood that the piece had found its true meaning. It was no longer simply the pizzica I had written, but a shared space. A Common Ground laid beneath our feet.
Experiences like this change you in subtle but lasting ways. The energy they transmit, the enthusiasm, the renewed sense of trust in the future�all of it remains.
A few years ago, I was in Adelaide to perform at WOMAD with Justin Adams, and the night before our concert I had the chance to attend a performance by Billy Bragg. At one point, he said something that has stayed with me ever since: �Music does not have the power to change the world. But it can make you believe that the world can be changed.�

Blogfoolk

items.body:
How do you celebrate 50 years of music by a band that blazed trails for the charged, hypnotic pizzica sound, breaking it out of its homeland in southern Italy? How do you look afresh at a sound that�s changed and broadened its appeal without ever abandoning its roots as a new generation took over the instruments? It�s a challenge, but what Canzionere Grecanico Salentino (CGS) have done is reframe some of the pieces from those earlier decades through the lens of those playing and singing the songs now.
The brainchild of Rina and Daniele Durante, early CGS avidly proudly staked out its territory as champions of an almost forgotten culture. In the hands of their son, fiddler/frame drummer and singer Mauro Durante, the original vision has gone global (he also has a successful duo with guitarist Justin Adams) and they�ve become a major name in world music for their energy and outstanding musicality. They�ve made people in so many countries believe in the pizzica. One big milestone acceptance came with working alongside the celebrated pianist Ludovico Einaudi on his
Taranta
project in 2014, which gave them an even wider reach and boosted them even high. Very aptly, a remix and remastering of the �Taranta� track with him is included.
In a world that loves to dance, this is dance music with depth and power that explodes out of the speakers. It honors the material from the past while keeping its eyes firmly fixed on the future, clasping hands across the generations to celebrate the band and its lauded history.
Il Mito
(The Myth) pays homage without ever being slavish. There�s a real, urgent energy to the music-making here.
The title cut was written by the older Durantes, a cornerstone of CGS�s early repertoire and a reflection on life in their part of Italy. Roberto Licci comes to sing with his son Emanuele. Early vocalist Rossella Pinto reprises her role on �Lu Rusciu De Lu Mare.� Yet this isn�t all hearkening to the past. The sounds have taken on new colors and arrangements as younger fingers play them. It�s still mostly acoustic, with a few electric touches like a synth bass to round out the sound.
This is still completely Italian music, the enveloping, dry sound of pizzica, something that�s evolved over the last half-century, moving from a regional to a global stage. The band, and their compositions, deserve the party, but it begs the question:
Where will all this be in another 50 years?

items._cn_summary: 专辑庆祝Canzionere Grecanico Salentino乐队成立五十周年，核心策略是将乐队早期作品以当代视角重新编排演绎。由家族第二代小提琴手兼手鼓手Mauro Durante主导，乐队在保留意大利南部pizzica音乐干燥而强烈的声学特质之余，加入了合成器贝斯等少量电声元素，使传统旋律获得新的色彩与层次。专辑还收录了与钢琴家Ludovico Einaudi合作的'Taranta'项目混音版本，并邀请了乐队创始成员Rina与Daniele Durante的原版作品演唱者回归，实现跨世代的声音对话。整体制作以原声乐器为主，电声点缀恰到好处，既致敬历史又指向未来，是一部将地方性民间传统推向全球舞台的能量之作。

items.body: W�R, Kongero - Songbooks Live by Nordic Notes This collaboration between the five-piece Belgian instrumental group W�r, whose members specialize in bringing the music of earlier centuries to life, and Kongero, the acclaimed Swedish female acapella folk quartet, offers an unusual chance to explore how their two cultures, ostensibly so different, can come together. It might sounds an unlikely mix, but here�s a spoiler: it turns out they�re pretty much musical best friends. The album kicks off at a cracking pace with �Var �r Du?�, a bravura performance through a twisted, tortuous piece that manages to be both elegant and surprising. However, the true astonishment arrives at the end, when the audience applauds and you suddenly realize this was recorded live (actually over two separate performances). W�R, Kongero - Songbooks Live by Nordic Notes The musicians bring material from their separate traditions, plus one original, showcasing their skills in intricate, swinging arrangements for both instruments and voices. Thanks to their skill, the varied ideas fit together seamlessly so it�s brimming with delights, like the wonderfully-titled �Drinking Like A Sweet Swede,� where the singers layers their harmonies over a jaunty backing. Everything is intricate, performed with a glowing precision that can disarm the senses with its beauty. The highlight, perhaps, is the beautiful �Klosterjungfrun.� The slow, seductive opening draws in the listener, the voices airy and light, curling around each other as the instruments wind long their path their. It�s a beautiful piece, but really, just one gem among so many here. W�R, Kongero - Songbooks Live by Nordic Notes There�s never a foot wrong, no note out of place and the performances are passionate, stellar, a true collaboration of instruments and voices. Add to that a mix that�s sharp as a razor, and Songbooks Live is a truly outstanding album, a perfect illustration that people have more in common than separates them. And it illustrates exactly what artists can achieve live. With luck, they�ll work together again. Soon, please. Find the artists online. items.body: Echo by Emi Makabe L oss galvanizes, loss focuses, and musical artists turn loss into shared reflections. Emi Makabe has focused the passing of her father into a generous meditation on resilience and legacy with her second recording on Sunnyside Records, Echo . The title reminds us of the connections between generations. Here are ten musical memories that span time and culture, blending a modern jazz sensibility with a traditional Japanese soul. Born in Japan, where she studied Japanese traditional music, Emi Makabe moved to New York in 2008. She is an educator and contributor to the jazz scene, composing and performing her own music. Her previous recordings, an EP on the Japanese Jazz label D-Musica Out of Time (2016) and Anniversary (2020), laid the foundation of her sound: soaring, sweet singing in Japanese, English and wordless vocalizing, accompanied by her flute and shamisen on top of jazz-inspired piano, drums, and double bass. Using these materials, Makabe celebrates the legacy of her father, supported by Thomas Morgan (double bass, backing vocals) and Vitor Gon�alves (piano, accordion, Wurlitzer electric piano), both of whom return from her previous records, as well as Kenny Wollesen (drums, percussion, vibraphone, electronics). Also appearing as guests are Meshell Ndegeocello (spoken word), Jason Moran (piano), and Bill Frisell (acoustic guitar) on the opening track. Echo by Emi Makabe Opening with Frisell�s acoustic guitar and confidently sentimental, �Birthday Song� comes to grips with loss, featuring a touching spoken meditation and a haunting Frisell solo. It ends with the hope, �I wanna remember the warmth of being in your arms.� The record closes with �Overture,� anchored by Gon�alves� dripping Wurlitzer supporting Makabe�s Japanese exhortation, �Let's talk again, countless times/Let's talk, if we meet again.� Echo by Emi Makabe Besides the refreshingly unselfconscious sentimentality, Makabe strides confidently between the traditional Japanese melodies, instruments, and the language of her upbringing in her father�s world and the contemporary jazz of New York clubs. �Snow� begins with Makabe�s shamisen playing a pentatonic tune, while �Text� swings in a fast bebop, with Makabe�s flute and harmonized Japanese scat singing. Echo by Emi Makabe �Morisan� hurries between worlds led by bouncy accordion, rolling jazz traps, and a stylish piano solo by Jason Moran. Moran also shares production credits with Thomas Morgan and Makabe herself. Utterly unique in approach, and equipped with a lovely vocal instrument, and with a skilled and single-minded ensemble, Emi Makabe has created a passionate, introspective, and honest fusion of tradition and modernity to celebrate the passing of the generations. Find the artist online. Further listening: Carmen Souza - The Silver Messengers: A Tribute to Horace Silver Mamak Khadem - Rembrance Yussef Dayes - Black Classical Music

items._cn_summary: Emi Makabe的第二张专辑以父亲离世为核心主题，将个人追思转化为跨越时空与文化的音乐冥想。专辑以现代爵士为骨架，融合日本传统三味线、笛子与日语演唱，同时辅以钢琴、低音提琴和鼓构成的爵士节奏组。Bill Frisell在开场曲中的原声吉他勾勒出温情感伤氛围，Meshell Ndegeocello的口白加入深化了沉思感。Jason Moran的钢琴独奏与跳跃的手风琴在不同曲目中穿梭于传统五声音调与bebop即兴之间，Wurlitzer电钢琴为终曲赋予怀旧光泽。制作由Moran、Thomas Morgan与Makabe共同完成，编排在传统与现代之间取得平衡。这张作品以真诚的情感表达和东西方音乐语汇的自然交织，展现了独特的跨文化美学视角。

items.body:
Echospace Detroit’s Stephen Hitchell is at his most romantic, club-friendly and elemental on these effortless dub house glyders, newly remastered by Pole for posterity and optimal immersion

Originally issued on 12” in 2015 and hard-to-find ever since, ‘Lost Sequence’ is classic, archetypal Echospace tackle. The OG goes for 14 mins of strutting deep house groove swaddled in velvet-coated textures dubbed to the rafters and happy to hold its lane for the duration, adding extra layers of conga and crackling atmosphere as it proceeds. Hitchell’s Intrusion dub pitches the same elements in a spring weather system, drenching everything in fine mist of elemental FX and loosening the bass drum to a satisfyingly soggy slosh for 16 minutes of hypnotic bliss out.
items._genre: dub house / dub techno / ambient house / deep house
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Echospace Detroit核心成员Stephen Hitchell的dub house作品，原版2015年以12寸黑胶发行后一度难寻，由德国电子音乐人Pole重新母带处理。整张作品围绕两条线索展开：原曲以14分钟的纵深house律动为骨架，铺满丝绒质感的dub回声层与打击乐纹理；Intrusion dub混音则将相同素材解构，浸入细密的环境效果与松散的鼓机节奏中，形成16分钟的低催眠流动。整体制作思路强调空间感与频率层次的控制，在节奏与氛围之间维持平衡。

items.body: Kr�ta , the latest release on Norway's Taragot label, features a Swede and two Norwegians playing interpretations of mainly traditional tunes from their respective countries. Fiddler Mats Ed�n has long been involved in Swedish folk music, as a player, composer and teacher, and in the process exploring and integrating different musical styles and approaches. Tellef Kvifte was in the pioneering Norwegian crossover band Slinkombas in the 1970s and has continued to play a central role in Norwegian folk music, both as a musician and an academic. Most often heard playing the sj�fl�yte , more widely known as a recorder, Kvifte has employed other instruments from outside the Norwegian tradition, in particular the saxophone and bagpipes. His son Knut Kvifte Nesheim , a drummer and composer, has also shown a determination to blur the lines between different musical genres, both in his solo and group projects. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio It comes as no surprise then to find this trio offering a far from conventional take on the tunes they have chosen. While dance tunes may be the source of most of the material here, this feels more akin to chamber music; not that it is remotely classical in style, but in the sense it conveys of three players engrossed in a musically intimate conversation. This is not a performance appropriate for accompanying dancers but might instead be seen as an exploration of hidden possibilities of meaning in the music. In so doing it reveals some of its underlying mystery, including, perhaps, a darker side. Just as in an Ibsen play, where the surface bonhomie, jollity and social nicety can be hiding something more sinister, in Scandinavian dance music there are at times hints of a troublesome undercurrent below the surface. So the decision to open proceedings with �Fossgrimen,� a fiddle tune from Norway's Setesdal valley, is perhaps significant. A fossgrimen is a mythical creature, a kind of water-sprite living in waterfalls from whom fiddle-players were considered to have learned their skills and for that were not universally welcomed, with the fiddle considered to be the devil's instrument. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio Tellef Kvifte takes the lead melody on most tracks but on the Swedish �Polska from Per Myhr,� having played a repeated introductory riff on the sj�fl�yte, with Mats Ed�n providing an amorphous textural accompaniment below and Nesheim adding some quiet tinkling, it's Ed�n who introduces the tune on the fiddle with Kvifte proceeding to play in unison. It's a short track and almost as soon as it gets going things start to fragment and everything grind to a halt.

items.body: Alison Cotton The Gods Laugh A relative's death leads the English viola player and vocalist to a meditation on grief and rebirth, backed by a soundscape of drones and crows The Gods Laugh by Alison Cotton John Clare’s poem I Am is a rumination on the scaly underbelly of human existence: feelings of despair and loneliness (“I am the self-consumer of my woes”). items._cn_summary: 英国中提琴手兼歌手 Alison Cotton 的专辑《The Gods Laugh》以亲人离世为创作起点，将个人悲痛转化为对生命循环的沉思。整张作品以绵延的低音持续音（drone）和乌鸦的田野录音构建出阴沉而冥想式的声场，中提琴的人声化演奏与歌唱交织，营造出介于室内乐与民谣之间的氛围。第二轨直接借用英国诗人约翰·克莱尔（John Clare）诗作《I Am》中的意象，标题则暗示对残酷神性的反思。专辑跨越了当代古典、实验民谣与氛围音乐之间的边界，器乐处理方式具有实验性，但整体仍保留较强的可听性与抒情内核，适合喜欢慢速冥想型音乐的听众。

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — The Boston-based band's eighth studio album release since 2007.1. "Sigil To Ruin" (10:33) ambient space synths open this one before infinity electric guitar notes emerge from the depths to be joined by the complement of syncopated heavy rock walls of sound. This start leads to a cool atmospheric break at the two-minute mark which is followed by a more humane motif with Nicholas DiSalvo's augmented post-Tim Smith MIDLAKE-like vocals. This is really nice! I really like bassist Jack Donovan's sound and playing just above Georg Edert's syncopated rock drumming, just below Nicholas' rhythm guitar work. The chorus buildup is more like a return to the guitar-heavy opening. Cool synth and guitar effects in the sixth minute woven beneath the vocals. The eighth minute has a nice diversion of jagged, mathematical Synth Pop chords before guitar and vocals join in to ground it more in straight-line movement. Then the music gets djenty for the exposure of a nice little rock guitar solo. Though all of the musicians feel skilled, no one seems to be trying to out-perform the others--and there are very few overtly "solo" exhibitions. An impressive and likable opener if a bit regimented. (18.125/20)2. "Capture/Release" (8:47) a gentle, prolonged cinematic synthesizer "space" introduction takes us to the addition of staccato notes and swirling spirals of waves from keyboards before the band launches into a nice two chord motif for the second minute. Enter lead vocalist Nicholas DeSalvo with a voice(s) and harmonized vocal sound that reminds me quite a bit of both John Young's LIFESIGNS and Belgian-based international supergroup FISH ON FRIDAY. The music continues to flow like a Post Rock band using a 1980s and 1990s techno/New Wave sound palette. The sound palette thickens and gets heavier in the second half--not unlike some of the walls of sound Jared Leach created on his masterful 2016 GHOST MEDICINE release, Discontinuance. Despite taking us on a fairly straightforward ride, the music is always easy to enjoy, the scenery evoked pleasant. (18.125/20)3. "Through Zero" (9:06) cool heavily-reverbed electric guitar opening reminds me of both THE CURE and KINGSTON WALL but it quickly turns heavier, sounding more like some of the grungy metal of the 1990s (which is not quite as much to my liking as the opening). But this turns djenty as a lead guitarist solos over it until 1:25 when a two-guitar chord arpeggiation opens things up for Nicholas to enter with a Kevin Moore (Chroma Key)-like lead vocal to enter. The driving effect of the Georg's drumming is quite solid, even as the song takes a couple of detours, left and right, over the next minute or two. The motif that is held in the fifth minute is quite nice: something that really piques my interest. This is developed with searing infinity electric guitar notes and complex harmonized vocals until the band returns to the uber-heavy wall of sound for the seventh minute. Nice work in the complex weave of the eighth minute: bass, drums, and two guitars holding fast to their places in the weave. (17.75/20)4. "Strata" (10:48) opening with alternating bass notes and keyboard arpeggio moving through a few chords together--again reminding me of both THE CURE but also the COCTEAU TWINS--before launching into a very cool almost KITCHENS OF DISTINCTION/early THE FIXX/ALAN PARSONS PROJECT motif with THE BUGGLES-like flat-toned robot-like harmony vocals on top. The instrumental passages between the vocal verses return to the CURE/COCTEAU motif of the opening section--which is really cool--and, eventually, include ICEHOUSE-like vocals on top, existing as the chorus. At the end of the fourth minute a searing JARED LEACH-like weave of twin lead guitars joins in, giving the music a much more grungy ALICE IN CHAINS/PEARL JAM-like feel and power--a wall of sound section that continues on well into the eighth minute. Around 7:15 the bass and drums let up on the gas a bit but the thick walls of sound continue and somebody's lead guitar solo intensifies until 8:10 when the whole soundscape switches dimensions, now chugging along to make more space for the return of Nicholas' vocals to re-enter around the 9:00 mark. Definitely my favorite weaves on the album so far. (18.25/20)5. "Sight Unseen" (8:50) opening with a much longer and more spacious, even proggy, buildup and transitory weave than we've seen/heard on this album before, it becomes still fairly thick but highly melodic and almost electronic/Kosmische, especially in the second motif (which starts around the 3:20 mark) with a lead synth melody pattern dominating the four-or-five-instrument Math Rock-like weave. Another solid song even if it is only instrumental and only three prolonged motifs (with basically one speed coming from drummer Gerog Edert) drawn out over the nine minutes. The third motif (which slowly establishes itself in the seventh minute) is like a heavy, grungy Ozric Tentacles, but this very suddenly cuts out, allowing a space-atmospheric keyboard patch to fill the sonosphere for the final minute. (17.625/20)6. "Blighted Age" (5:48) opening with picked acoustic guitars within which Nicolas joins in with a COLIN BLUNSTONE-like vocal sound and style. The music develops just like something from Kevin Moore's CHROMA KEY's albums from the turn of the century. This would actually have been one of the best songs from either Dead Air for Radios or You Go Now. There's just this haunting brainworm quality to the sound palette and repetitive chord progression used. Awesome song! (9.333/10)Total time: 53:52They're still heavy but they might be a little more proggy, a little more prone to atmospheric and melodic passages than before.A-/4.5 stars; an excellent and very solid and consistent heavy prog that displays nicely disciplined musicianship as well as exquisitely-forged compositions.

items._cn_summary: 德国爵士钢琴家Joachim Kühn 1969年在汉堡录制的专辑《Sound Of Feelings》，由法国BYG Records旗下Actuel系列发行，属于欧洲自由爵士场景的重要文献。专辑共七首作品，全部由Kühn作曲，收录曲时长从三分钟到八分钟不等。演奏编制以钢琴为核心，搭配贝斯、鼓、长笛、铃铛、铃鼓等多种乐器，Kühn本人还演奏中音萨克斯、唢呐与手铃，展现出多乐器即兴的探索倾向。专辑包含一首John Coltrane作品《Wellcome》，呼应了六十年代末自由爵士的精神脉络。BYG Actuel系列是当时欧洲前卫音乐的重要厂牌之一，录音在汉堡Windrose Studio完成。该资料页主要呈现唱片版本信息与曲目列表，缺乏对音乐本体与演奏特征的实质性评述。
